newsitem.title: USA: P&U gets U.S. FDA clearance to market Dostinex.
newsitem.headline: P&U gets U.S. FDA clearance to market Dostinex.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said Thursday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market Dostinex (cabergoline) tablets for the treatment of hyperprolactinemic disorders.
Dostinex will be available in March 1997, the company said.

Hyperprolactinemia is usually caused by a benign tumor on the pituitary gland that results in excess production of prolactin, the hormone that controls lactation. The company said doctors treat from 70,000 to 100,000 patients with the condition each year, the vast majority women.

The condition most commonly affects women ages 20 to 50 years, and can cause cessation of menstruation, excessive breast milk discharge and infertility. In men, the condition can cause decreased libido and impotence, the company said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn said Sandoz AG makes the only other drug product, Parlodel (bromocriptine), indicated to treat hyperprolactinemia.
Pharmacia & Upjohn said its tests showed Dostinex outperformed the Sandoz product, and two doses a week are required for Dostinex, compared to one to three doses daily for bromocriptine.
Sandoz officials could not be reached for comment.

Pharmacia & Upjohn said clinical trials with about 450 patients showed prolactin levels returned to normal in 77 percent of patients treated with Dostinex. Restoration of menses occurred in 77 percent of women treated with Dostinex, the company said.
Among patients with excessive breast milk discharge, the symptom disappeared in 73 percent of those treated with Dostinex, the company said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn, a research-based pharmaceutical company, has a corporate management center in London and major research and manufacturing centers in the United States, Sweden and Italy.
